description.value: The study compared automated FreeSurfer and semi-automated CMA brain segmentation methods for measuring regional brain volumes in alcoholic and nonalcoholic control subjects.

Four groups of subjects participated in this study, including alcoholic and nonalcoholic male and female cohorts. Participants were recruited from advertisements and flyers and underwent MRI and neuropsychological testing.

Brain morphometry is the study of neuroanatomical structures with the use of volumetric analyses.
gray matter, white matter, and ventricles were segmented

Measures of regional brain volumes, which can be derived from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) images by dividing a brain into its constituent parts, can be used as structural indicators of many different neuroanatomical diseases and disorders, including alcoholism.
The volumes obtained from the CMA and FreeSurfer methods were converted to a common metric unit (mL).

The QFI between the male alcoholics and female alcoholics (not shown) was significant (P = 0.034).Abbreviations: MALC, male alcoholic; FALC, female alcoholic; MNC, male normal control; FNC, female normal control; QFI, quantity frequency index.

caption.value: Common mean volume of structures across both methods (in mL) for 69 pairs of volume estimates, along with per-subject differences from the common mean (in volume and percentage volume);

footer.value: Note: The test statistic is given for the hypothesis that the average volume difference is 0, as an indicator of difference in the measurement. Positive values indicate the CMA volume is greater than the FreeSurfer volume. The ICC is given for the assumption of the consistency of volumes between methods (see text for details). Abbreviations: CMA, Center for Morphometric Analysis; ICC, intraclass correlation coefficient.

caption.value: Average PCVD between the methods in directional (top) and absolute (bottom) terms (see text for details);

footer.value: Notes: Test statistics are given for the ANOVA model fitting each subject’s PCVD by the factors group (alcoholic, control), sex (male, female), and their interaction. (P-values greater than 0.15 are not shown.) For the directional shown.) For the directional PCVD, positive values indicate the CMA volume estimate is larger than the FreeSurfer volume estimate.Abbreviations: CMA, Center for Morphometric Analysis; PCVD, percent common volume difference.
